_readme: Round 4 of 7 — big august 9th batch (in-copyright PDFs). 24 of 25 books processed; The Algebra of Infinite Justice (Arundhati Roy) excluded — PDF appears to be scanned/image-only, no extractable text layer, flagged for retry. Synopses grounded in real detect.mjs-extracted text; mentions curated from candidates.json per docs/detector.md exclusion rules; genres per tools/genres.mjs.

books.title: Outer Dark
books.author: Cormac McCarthy
books.synopsis: In backwoods Appalachia, Culla Holme fathers a child with his sister Rinthy and abandons it in the woods, telling her it died; when she discovers the truth and sets off searching for the baby and the tinker who took it, Culla wanders separately through a landscape of hangings, a turpentine camp, and a marauding trio of drifters who eventually murder the child before Culla's eyes.

books.title: Pachinko
books.author: Min Jin Lee
books.synopsis: A multigenerational saga following a Korean family, beginning with Sunja, a fisherman's daughter in Japanese-occupied Korea who bears a child out of wedlock, as they emigrate to Osaka and struggle across decades as ethnic Korean outsiders in Japan, with sons Noa and Mozasu taking divergent paths through education and the pachinko business.

books.title: Paradise
books.author: Toni Morrison
books.synopsis: A group of armed men from the all-Black town of Ruby, Oklahoma raid a nearby former convent to kill or drive out the women sheltering there, and the novel moves between the men's rationalizations, voiced partly through Reverend Richard Misner's doubts about the town's hardening insularity, and the convent women's interwoven backstories, closing on an ocean vision of a woman named Piedade singing to a rescued companion.

books.title: Patrimony: A True Story
books.author: Philip Roth
books.synopsis: Philip Roth recounts the final two years of his elderly father Herman Roth's life in Elizabeth, New Jersey, from the 1989 diagnosis of a brain tumor through a decision against surgery, a swallowing crisis, and his death, interwoven with Newark childhood stories, the family shaving mug, and Roth's own emergency heart bypass during the same period.

books.title: People of the Book
books.author: Geraldine Brooks
books.synopsis: Book conservator Hanna Heath is brought to Sarajevo to examine and stabilize the illuminated Sarajevo Haggadah after it is rescued from the museum, and the physical clues she finds in its binding and stains, an insect wing, wine stains, salt, a white hair, trigger interleaved historical narratives tracing the manuscript's path back through Vienna, Venice, Tarragona, and fifteenth-century Seville.

books.title: A Promised Land
books.author: Barack Obama
books.synopsis: Obama's memoir of his early political rise and first term as president, covering the 2008 campaign, the financial crisis, the fight for healthcare reform, and decisions like the raid on bin Laden, told through detailed behind-the-scenes accounts of White House deliberations.

books.title: Reading Like a Writer
books.author: Francine Prose
books.synopsis: A close-reading guide for writers and readers that works word by word, sentence by sentence, and paragraph by paragraph through passages from classic and contemporary fiction to show how great prose actually functions, drawing constantly on named authors from Chekhov to Nabokov.

books.title: Reamde
books.author: Neal Stephenson
books.synopsis: A sprawling techno-thriller that follows a MMORPG-spawned ransomware virus called REAMDE as it drags a games executive, his niece, Russian mobsters, and Islamist militants into a globe-spanning chase across British Columbia, China, and the Philippines.

books.title: Rich Dad Poor Dad for Teens: The Secrets About Money
books.author: Robert T. Kiyosaki
books.synopsis: An adaptation of Kiyosaki's financial-education framework for a teen audience, using the contrasting lessons of his own 'rich dad' and 'poor dad' to argue for financial literacy, asset ownership, and entrepreneurship over conventional schooling and salaried work.

books.title: Rich People Problems
books.author: Kevin Kwan
books.synopsis: The final novel of the Crazy Rich Asians trilogy, centered on the Singaporean Young/Shang family's scramble over the deathbed and inheritance of matriarch Su Yi, mixing satire of ultra-wealthy excess with Nick and Rachel's efforts to reconcile with his estranged family.

books.title: SPQR: A History of Ancient Rome
books.author: Mary Beard
books.synopsis: Mary Beard traces Roman history from the legendary founding by Romulus and the semi-mythical kings through the political crises of the Republic, opening with Cicero's suppression of the Catiline conspiracy, and on through the rise of the emperors and the Roman world beyond the city, ending around 212 CE.

books.title: Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind
books.author: Yuval Noah Harari
books.synopsis: Harari surveys the history of Homo sapiens from the Cognitive Revolution through the Agricultural Revolution, the unification of humankind under empires, money, and religion, and the Scientific Revolution, closing with speculation about the species' technological future.

books.title: Secret Son
books.author: Laila Lalami
books.synopsis: Raised by his mother in a one-room house in the slums of Casablanca, Youssef El Mekki discovers that the father he believed dead is alive and wealthy, moves into his new family's world of privilege, and then, after a reversal of fortune sends him back to the streets, is drawn into a fringe Islamist organization known as the Party.

books.title: Seveneves
books.author: Neal Stephenson
books.synopsis: When the moon inexplicably blows apart, humanity has roughly two years before the fragments will bombard Earth and scour it lifeless, forcing a scramble to build a Cloud Ark of orbiting habitats around the space station Izzy; the story later jumps five thousand years to the descendants of seven survivors who have rebuilt a society in a habitat ring.

books.title: Shalimar the Clown
books.author: Salman Rushdie
books.synopsis: In the Kashmiri village of Pachigam, the clown and tightrope walker Shalimar marries the dancer Boonyi, whose affair with the American ambassador Max Ophuls sets off a chain of betrayal and revenge that turns Shalimar into an assassin and eventually entangles Max's daughter Kashmira in Los Angeles.

books.title: Shame
books.author: Salman Rushdie
books.synopsis: In the border town of Q. and later in the corridors of power of a thinly veiled Pakistan, the fates of General Raza Hyder, the Prime Minister Iskander Harappa, and Hyder's shame-driven daughter Sufiya Zinobia entangle with Omar Khayyam Shakil, a man born to three mother-sisters and raised without shame himself.

books.title: Shoe Dog: A Memoir by the Creator of Nike
books.author: Phil Knight
books.synopsis: Phil Knight recounts building Blue Ribbon into Nike, from an early-morning run through Oregon that opens the book, through importing Onitsuka running shoes from Japan, scouting factories, and fighting through cash crises, lawsuits, and boardroom betrayals to grow the company.

books.title: Snow
books.author: Orhan Pamuk
books.synopsis: The poet Ka travels to the snowbound Turkish city of Kars to investigate a wave of suicides among religious girls forbidden to wear headscarves, and gets swept into local political intrigue, a theatrical coup staged by the actor Sunay Zaim, and his own tangled love for Ipek and reunion with the revolutionary Fazil.

books.title: Snow Crash
books.author: Neal Stephenson
books.synopsis: In a balkanized near-future America run by corporate Burbclaves, pizza-delivery driver and part-time hacker the Deliverator and skateboard courier Y.T. get drawn into the spread of a mind-altering drug/virus called Snow Crash that threatens users in both the real world and the virtual Metaverse.

books.title: Stardust
books.author: Neil Gaiman
books.synopsis: Tristran Thorn, a young man from the village of Wall bordering the magical land of Faerie, crosses the wall to retrieve a fallen star to win his heart's desire, only to find the star is a living, injured young woman with her own dangers to escape.

books.title: Stella Maris
books.author: Cormac McCarthy
books.synopsis: A twenty-year-old doctoral candidate in mathematics checks herself into a psychiatric hospice in Black River Falls, Wisconsin, in 1972 carrying forty thousand dollars in cash, and her recorded sessions with a psychiatrist range across grief for her dead father and brother, her plans to disappear into the Romanian mountains, and long dialogues on Gödel, Spengler, and the foundations of mathematics.

books.title: Sula
books.author: Toni Morrison
books.synopsis: In the Bottom, a Black hill community above Medallion, Ohio, two girls, Nel and Sula, grow up inseparable before Sula leaves town for a decade of college and drifting; when she returns, her defiance of the community's moral codes, including sleeping with Nel's husband, turns her into the town's living embodiment of evil even as the novel traces the Peace and Wright family households across the decades.

books.title: Suttree
books.author: Cormac McCarthy
books.synopsis: Cornelius Suttree, who has abandoned a life of privilege, lives alone on a houseboat on the Tennessee River in Knoxville around 1950, fishing for a living and moving through a demimonde of prostitutes, junkmen, drunks, and petty criminals like Gene Harrogate, in a sequence of episodes marked by arrests, illness, and sudden violent death.

books.title: Terminal Man
books.author: Michael Crichton
books.synopsis: Harry Benson, a computer scientist who suffers blackout seizures and violent rages after a car accident left him with psychomotor epilepsy, undergoes an experimental operation at a Los Angeles hospital to implant a computer that delivers electrical stimulation to his brain to suppress his attacks; when the implant instead teaches him to trigger his own pleasurable seizures, he escapes the hospital and goes on a killing spree while doctors and police try to track him down.
